purpose: Identify the exact target and reconstruction objective
procedure: Record binary SHA-256, platform, build/region, loader, entry points and objective. Separate matching, readable reconstruction and porting. Preserve originals; choose a bounded first region.
exceptions: Never infer starting ABI or architecture solely from a filename.
acceptance: Input hashes and supported platform recorded.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Choose an independent runner. Record initial registers, memory permissions, files, clocks and external events. Replay twice. If behavior is nondeterministic, identify controls before comparing.
exceptions: Two executions of the same lifter are not independent.
acceptance: A replayable case and exact reference tool version.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Label each finding observed, inferred, tested or proved under a model. Link exact bytes, address, tool and source revision. Preserve contradictions. Require a discriminating check before promotion.
exceptions: Agreement among agents is not a test or proof.
acceptance: Claims retain scope and actual evidence links.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Inventory sections and images. Fetch mandatory dependencies explicitly; expand decisive sections; search for exceptions, obsolete versions and failed attempts. Record retrieved versus delivered and unresolved extraction gaps.
exceptions: Search snippets do not establish complete reading.
acceptance: Every declared critical obligation resolved or blocked.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Compare attempts and actual result hashes. Separate transport, environment, semantics, retrieval and reasoning failures. Ask the recovery reviewer for one discriminating experiment after repeated unchanged reasoning failures.
exceptions: Do not reload browsers to repair a reasoning failure.
acceptance: Next action distinguishes competing explanations.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Inspect callers, callee uses, stack effects, return uses, saved registers and exceptional exits. Propose ABI and parameter contracts with conflicting evidence. Test against reference calls.
exceptions: Names and prototypes are hypotheses until checked.
acceptance: Calling convention and effects tested on retained cases.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Group accesses by base and offset; distinguish unions, aliases, arrays and padding. Trace allocation sizes and constructor initialization. Preserve per-build offsets. Test reads and writes through all observed callers.
exceptions: One observed field offset is not a portable type layout.
acceptance: Proposed layout includes uncertainty and conflicting accesses.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

purpose: Recover control flow and unresolved targets
procedure: Map direct branches and calls; track indirect target provenance, jump tables and exception edges. Keep unresolved target sets explicit. Recover loops without using one trace as whole-program coverage.
exceptions: Unexecuted code may still be statically translated; traces are not complete coverage.
acceptance: Unknown edges remain visible and do not become dead code.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Identify dispatch tables, bytecode fetch, constants, stack/register VM state and resource boundaries. Separate script semantics from the native interpreter and version every format hypothesis.
exceptions: Native code recovery does not recover all game scripts or assets.
acceptance: At least one script input replays under the proposed model.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Declare integer widths, defined flags, memory spaces, endian/alignment, control state and faults. Execute supported raw P-code; stop on unknown user operations, FP/vector semantics or unmodeled effects.
exceptions: Never turn an unsupported instruction into a no-op.
acceptance: Positive and seeded negative differential cases pass.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Declare ABI, guest stack/memory, callbacks, external effects and ownership on both sides. Retain a working interpreter or emulator for unresolved regions. Test transitions in both directions.
exceptions: Original bytes alone are not a runtime fallback.
acceptance: Boundary tests and rollback preserve executable behavior.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

prerequisites: Exact candidate, reference, inputs and tools
procedure: Inspect required observations and initial-state contract; run independent reference and candidate; compare defined effects; retain first mismatch and replay input. Attempt proof only for supported complete regions.
exceptions: A finite differential pass is not all-input equivalence.
acceptance: Actual cases and proof assumptions attached to candidate hashes.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

purpose: Operate persistent Ghidra and REA projects
procedure: Use complete native foundations. Import once, record native program identity and revision, inspect before annotating, serialize conflicting writes, commit and save explicitly. Reconcile the operation ledger after lost acknowledgments.
exceptions: Do not overwrite user annotations or assume in-memory commit is durable save.
acceptance: Project reopens and operation identity is reconciled.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Read current hash. Retain before/after artifacts. Apply only with current epoch, expected revision and valid briefing. Run checks against resulting bytes. Retain unverified candidates separately.
exceptions: A stale worker may retain artifacts but cannot publish.
acceptance: Hashes, journal and save state agree.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

prerequisites: Authorized build recipe and evaluator boundary
procedure: Pin toolchain and recipe; retain command arguments, exit, output and artifact hashes. Run protected acceptance tests and seeded failures. Reject success claims without execution records.
exceptions: Timeouts and compiler exits are not passing results.
acceptance: Reproducible build and protected checks for exact candidate.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Declare goal, revision, method, uncertainty and checks. Adviser resolves required reading and supplies bounded procedure. Invalidate briefing after material evidence, contract or revision changes.
exceptions: Routine commands in a valid brief do not require redundant broad rereading.
acceptance: Intent, brief, evidence and execution are linked.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

purpose: Transfer work at a safe checkpoint
procedure: Reconcile pending effects; save state and evidence; preserve candidate edits; revoke old epoch then grant next writer. Restore exact revision and next action in the new session.
exceptions: Never hand off during an ambiguous native write.
acceptance: Old-writer rejection and restart recovery tests pass.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Restore known conversation/profile and durable message IDs. Search visible user messages for exact request marker. Reuse identity. If delivery remains ambiguous, quarantine without resending a mutation.
exceptions: A click is not proof of delivery; no duplicate blind retry.
acceptance: Recovered request/result hashes and actual external state agree.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

procedure: Propose one canonical knowledge/procedure/executable asset with overlapping applicability, conditions and counterexamples. Compare active and candidate on protected holdouts and regressions. Promote only measured gain; retain rollback.
exceptions: Origin is not applicability; identical-model claims are not independent evidence.
acceptance: Benefit and regression evidence linked to active version.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

purpose: Prepare a private or sanitized export
procedure: Build a fresh package from an explicit file allowlist. Exclude sources, browser profiles, credentials, private paths, host/account metadata and hidden evaluator data. Scan selected contents and keep unresolved items private.
exceptions: Secret links are not access control; never sanitize after public upload.
acceptance: Export manifest and scan precede publication.
sources: User design v3.0, sections 6–24 and Appendix C

purpose: Play-test a rebuilt game against its original
prerequisites: game.json play-testing contract, original image and candidate build manifest
procedure: describe_game first. Reach the situation with a named start or short play_game steps (state numbers first, frames second). Compare with side both or test_game compare; never steer around a divergence during a comparison. Explore with a recorded seed when targets are unknown. Shrink each finding, read its bug package, fix the earliest divergence first, then rerun regressions and explore again. Save shrunk findings as regressions.
exceptions: A problem the original reproduces with the same trajectory is original behavior.
An unreached start, a harness limit or a cancelled run is not a pass.
Exploration that finds nothing is sampled evidence, not proof of correctness.
acceptance: Trajectory tokens for every finding and fix; pinned game_play checks pass on the rebuilt candidate.
sources: Visual Game Testing Proposal v0.1 and dev/GAME_TESTING.md (v0.2)
evidence_strength: design-derived; executable harness tests listed separately
